chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not prescribe for women any makeup (of missed prayers or fasts) nor any fasting other than the fasting of Ramadan, unless it is a vow or voluntary (fasting).
ai.seo_question: Do women need to make up missed prayers or fasts in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling to clarify the distinction between obligatory (*fard*) and voluntary (*nafl*) acts for women, emphasizing that missed obligatory prayers must be made up while missed voluntary fasts do not. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that women's exemption from certain compensatory acts stems from the natural burdens of menstruation and childbirth, which are considered valid excuses for missing voluntary acts but not the core pillar of prayer. The narration underscores the principle that religious obligations are tailored to individual capacity, reinforcing the balance between divine command and human ease.
